claim_summary: SCENARIODIFF turns noisy, weakly aligned documents into three levels of frozen-LLM guidance (stepwise context summaries, a horizon-level scenario description, sparse anchor intervals) that condition a diffusion forecaster, and refines its trajectories at inference through Anchor Blended Sampling.

claim_evidence.quote: condition a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer, while Anchor Blended Sampling locally refines generated trajectories without retraining.

modules.name: Historical context summarization agent
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: the summary compresses documents aligned to each observed timestep and has no forecasting output requirement, so it is not bound to the task. R3_2_GTS yes: it depends on timestep alignment and information availability (only documents aligned with observed timesteps). Counterfactual: a change of task family would not require redesigning the summaries.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - summaries compress aligned documents with no task output requirement
R3_2_GTS:yes - depends on timestep alignment and information availability

evidence.quote: We therefore use a frozen Historical Context Agent to compress each local document set into a concise summary.
These summaries provide a temporally grounded semantic view of the observed history and serve as the main textual representation of past evidence.

modules.name: Scenario description agent
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: the agent produces a description of expected future behavior over the forecast horizon, which embeds the forecasting output requirement. Counterfactual: a change to another task family would require redesigning the scenario output.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - horizon-level scenario description embeds the forecasting output requirement

evidence.quote: We introduce a frozen Scenario Agent, which generates a scenario description from the observed history
The scenario description is a short natural-language statement about expected future behavior, such as overall direction, volatility, or likely disruptions.

modules.name: Anchor guidance agent
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: the agent outputs time-indexed value intervals over future timesteps L+1 to L+H, so the forecasting output requirement is embedded. Counterfactual: a different task family would need different anchor semantics.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - anchor intervals are indexed to future forecast timesteps

evidence.quote: where abrupt changes may occur. We therefore introduce an Anchor Guidance Agent, which converts the available context into sparse anchor points for inference-time guidance.

modules.name: Anchor Blended Sampling
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: the distance-to-band objective over future anchor intervals is the validation criterion of the forecasting task; the blended refinement checks and corrects the trajectory within one forecast episode. Counterfactual: a different task family would require a different refinement objective.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - distance-to-band objective over future anchor intervals is the forecasting validation criterion

evidence.quote: editing stage. Anchor Blended Sampling refines this source trajectory by editing anchor-relevant regions while preserving the remaining temporal structure.

modules.name: Scenario-conditioned multimodal diffusion forecaster
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: the denoising target is the clean future horizon and the forecaster is a forecasting model in the Tools and Execution sense. Counterfactual: changing the task family (for example to imputation) would require redesigning the masked target and loss. Not an LLM, so not LLM side (R2).
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - denoising target is the future horizon; redesign needed for other task families

notes: Scope: frozen LLM agents (Gemini 2.5 Flash, prompt-only, no parameter update) are Harness; no LLM-side module is contributed. The diffusion forecaster is a trained numerical model, not an LLM; it is classified as a TSK forecasting model under Tools and Execution, a borderline call that the adjudicator should confirm (drop module diffusion if the forecaster is judged outside the harness). Historical context agent is GTS because it is not bound to the forecasting objective; the other agents are TSK because their outputs are indexed to the future horizon. No temporal function is recorded for TSK modules; the history-only input that avoids leakage is treated as a design property, not a validation function. Evaluation: only forecasting error and CRPS are reported; no process trace or decision-utility evidence. Table quotes avoid the spaced small-caps method name in the packet.
